h1: Khum Damnoen Resort — Balinese villas by the Damnoen Saduak Floating Market, with a 70 m saltwater pool
intro: Picture a Balinese resort set among Ratchaburi's orchards, with a saltwater pool running the length of the grounds, so close to the Damnoen Saduak Floating Market you can paddle a boat to it — Khum Damnoen Resort delivers that picture at a price you can reach · Opened in 2018 on more than 7 rai ringed by local orchards, it's split into a hotel zone, a villa zone and a jacuzzi-villa zone · The highlight is a roughly 70 m saltwater pool running through the middle of the resort, with a kids' pool and a jacuzzi · Many villas have a private outdoor jacuzzi · Rooms start from around ฿2,150/night on weekdays — a sharp deal for a good-looking villa near the floating market.

body.html: Damnoen Saduak is famous for the floating market travellers worldwide want to see at least once, yet good places to stay in the area are surprisingly few — and Khum Damnoen Resort is the name that comes up most among resorts near the market · The idea here was to build a Balinese-style resort on more than 7 rai, ringed by orchards and a natural canal, open since 2018 · Step inside and it feels like leaving the city for another world: leafy, quiet, and finished in the natural wood and stone of Bali, which guests say photographs beautifully from every angle.

The resort is split into three main zones — a hotel zone, a villa zone and a jacuzzi-villa zone — for about 47 rooms in total · There are several room types, from Villa Room and Lake Villa (looking out over the canal) to Villa Jacuzzi and Lake Jacuzzi, which come with a private outdoor jacuzzi · The villas are decorated in Balinese style, with soft beds, strong air-con, bathrobes and room service · Many guests describe the Lake Villa as a dream-like room, where you can sit by the canal in front of your villa all day.
"Incredible service, clean room, wonderful nature, and really close to the floating market — just around the corner; you can even take a boat there."

The highlight everyone mentions is the roughly 70 m saltwater pool that runs through the middle of the resort · It's split into an adult pool, a kids' pool and a jacuzzi corner, open round the clock · Saltwater stings the eyes far less than chlorine, which suits children and anyone who swims for a while · Beyond the pool there's plenty to do — kayaking, SUP boarding, and free e-bikes to ride around the grounds, which families and groups love · There's a spa, a coffee shop, and an evening bar to relax by the water.

The food is another thing guests praise · The resort restaurant serves bold Thai cooking at prices many say are lower than expected for a resort this pretty — standout dishes include squid-roe soup, fried shrimp in tamarind sauce and a rice-noodle salad · There's a hot-pot set at around ฿699 · Some rooms even offer a floating breakfast served in your private pool for that picture-perfect shot · A fresh coconut welcome at check-in is a small touch guests like.

Location is the main reason people choose this place — it's in Damnoen Saduak District, very close to the Damnoen Saduak Floating Market, a few minutes' drive or a longtail boat ride from the resort · From Bangkok it's about 1.5-2 hours' drive, ideal for a weekend trip · The thing to know is that this area is all about quiet and nature: there are no shops or places to walk to right around the resort, so you'll need to drive to go anywhere · Real guest scores sit high at around 9.1 from over a hundred reviews on Trip.com, and Tripadvisor rates it 4 out of 5.

Honestly, Khum Damnoen Resort isn't a full five-star luxury resort, but it gives you a look and an atmosphere well beyond its price · The selling point is photogenic Balinese villas, the long saltwater pool, in-villa jacuzzis, plenty of activities and a location by the floating market, for low-two-thousands baht on weekdays · There are things to know, though: some reviews mention that certain hotel-zone rooms have no windows and have had damp issues · A few nights you may hear sound from a nearby temple or community event · And some walls are on the thin side · If you book, choose the villa zone or a Lake Villa, which are more open and better reviewed than the building rooms.

A tip from following the reviews here closely: pick a villa-zone room or a Lake Villa over the building rooms, as they give you the full open-air Balinese feel · If you're a group or a family, a villa with a jacuzzi near the pool is the best value · There's a fair gap between weekday and weekend rates (roughly ฿2,150 up to ฿4,800+ by room type and date), so compare a few platforms before booking · Wake up early and take the boat to the Damnoen Saduak Floating Market before the big tour groups arrive — that's when it's at its best.

honestSummary: Khum Damnoen Resort is the Balinese villa stay by the Damnoen Saduak Floating Market that gives you a look and feel beyond its price — a 70 m saltwater pool, in-villa jacuzzis, plenty of activities, good service and tasty, affordable food, for low-two-thousands baht on weekdays · It isn't a full five-star resort, some hotel-zone rooms have no windows and there's nothing to walk to around it, but for a relaxing stay by the floating market or a weekend out of Bangkok, it fits just right.
honestChecks: If you book a budget hotel-zone room — some have no windows and have had damp complaints → choose the villa zone or a Lake Villa, which are more open and better reviewed, if the budget allows.
If you want shops or somewhere to walk near the stay — the resort is ringed by orchards and a quiet community with nothing walkable → plan to drive out, or use the resort as a stay-put retreat.

If you're a light sleeper sensitive to noise — some nights bring temple or community sound, and some walls are thin → ask for a villa set deeper into the resort, and pick free cancellation just in case.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Khum Damnoen Resort, Ratchaburi

faq.q: Where is Khum Damnoen Resort and is it near the Damnoen Saduak Floating Market?
faq.a: It's at 50/1 Tha Nat, Damnoen Saduak District, Ratchaburi, very close to the Damnoen Saduak Floating Market — a few minutes' drive or a longtail boat ride from the resort · From Bangkok it's about 1.5-2 hours' drive, ideal for a weekend trip · Amphawa Floating Market is about 30 minutes away.

faq.q: How much does Khum Damnoen Resort cost and what room types are there?
faq.a: Rooms start from around ฿2,150/night on weekdays · There are several types — Lake Villa (from about ฿2,900), Villa Room (about ฿3,800), Lake Jacuzzi (about ฿3,900) and Villa Jacuzzi (about ฿4,800) with a private jacuzzi · Prices vary by room type and date, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: What pool and activities does Khum Damnoen Resort have?
faq.a: There's a roughly 70 m saltwater swimming pool running through the resort, split into an adult pool, a kids' pool and a jacuzzi · Plenty to do — kayaking, SUP boarding, free e-bikes around the grounds, a spa, and a boat ride to the floating market · Some rooms offer a floating breakfast served in a private pool.

It's best for couples, families and groups who want a relaxing Balinese-style resort near the floating market · You get photogenic villas, a saltwater pool, in-villa jacuzzis and plenty of activities at a reachable price · But there are no shops or places to walk to around the resort, so if you want an in-town stay with things within walking distance, look at the Ratchaburi town hotels instead.

faq.q: What are the review scores and what should I know?
faq.a: Real guest scores sit high at around 9.1 from over a hundred reviews on Trip.com, with Tripadvisor rating it 4 out of 5 · Common praise is for the pretty Balinese atmosphere, the long saltwater pool, good service, and tasty, affordable food near the market · Things to know: some hotel-zone rooms have no windows and have had damp issues, some nights bring temple/community sound, and some walls are thin — choose the villa zone or a Lake Villa.
